history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: The CSV name 'Kali Mata Mandir' most plausibly refers to the Maa Dukh Bhanjani Kali Mata Temple at 151, Ghel Road, Ambala City - directory listings and visitor reviews for 'Kali Mata Mandir, Ghel Road' and 'Dukhbhanjani Kali Mata Temple, Opp. S.A. Jain College, Ghel Road' point to the same shrine (verify). The temple stands on a small island in the middle of Labhu Ka Talaab, a sacred pond, connected to the mainland by a small bridge. Per a single news article (OrangeNews9, UNVERIFIED), the black-stone Kali idol was originally worshipped in Sargodha district (now Pakistan); during Partition a devotee named Baba Phoolu Ram Ji brought it to Ambala, and following a dream installed it in the middle of the pond. Devotees believe five consecutive Saturday visits fulfil wishes, and milk abhishek during Navratri is believed to bless childless couples. The pond is currently reported dry and neglected in places (per visitor reviews).

town_description: Ambala is a major city in Haryana on the Punjab border, split into the twin hubs of Ambala City and Ambala Cantonment. It is one of North India's most important railway junctions, has a large military cantonment and Air Force presence, and is famous across India for its cloth and scientific-instrument markets. Tradition links the city's name to Goddess Amba (Bhawani Amba), whose ancient temple stands in the city.
